title: Normalized special coset for an immediate prime-degree extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be complete fields with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values [def-weil-field]. Write $F^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|$ for $F=K,L$. Assume $\widetilde K$ is algebraically closed, $\Gamma_K$ is divisible, $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde K>0$, $[L:K]=p$, $\widetilde L=\widetilde K$ and $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_K$. For a field $F$ with this absolute value, $a\in F$ and $s>0$, put $S_{a,s}(F)=\{c^p-ac+e:c,e\in F,\ |pc^p|<s,\ |e|<s\}$. A coset $b+S_{a,s}(F)$ is special if it does not contain zero, the infimum of the absolute values of its elements is $s$, and either $a=0$ or $(a,s)=(1,1)$. There exist $a\in\{0,1\}\subset K$, $s>0$ and $b\in K$ such that $b+S_{a,s}(K)$ is special and $0\in b+S_{a,s}(L)$. For every $v\in b+S_{a,s}(K)$ one has $|pv|<s=\inf_{c\in K}|c^p-ac+v|$ and there exists $\alpha\in L$ with $|\alpha^p-a\alpha+v|<s$. If $a=1$, one can instead take such an $\alpha$ satisfying $\alpha^p-\alpha+v=0$, and then $L=K(\alpha)$ as ordinary fields.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4(i)–(iii), printed p. 38; Lemma 6.1.2(i), printed p. 37; no tame base extension needed when the residue field is algebraically closed and the value group divisible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-immediate-minpoly-coefficient-preparation] to $L/K$, obtaining $\theta,r,R,f,b,a_i$. Put $s=r^p$. If $|a_1|=r^{p-1}$ put $A=-a_1$; otherwise put $A=0$. Then $g(T)=T^p-AT+b$ has $|A|\le r^{p-1}$ and either $A=0$ or $|A|=r^{p-1}$. The discarded coefficients have $|a_i|R^i<s$, including $i=1$ in the case where it is discarded. Thus $|f(x)-g(x)|<s$ for $|x|\le R$, in either $K$ or $L$. In particular $|g(\theta)|<s$ and $|p\theta^p|=|p|R^p<s$.

For $c\in K$ with $|c|\le R$, the preparation gives $|f(c)|=|\theta-c|^p>s$, hence $|g(c)|=|\theta-c|^p$. If $|c|>R$, then $|c|^p>|Ac|,|b|$ and $|\theta-c|=|c|$, so the same identity holds. Therefore $\inf_{c\in K}|g(c)|=r^p=s$, no value equals $s$, and $|pb|=|p|R^p<s$. These are numerical conclusions from the preparation, not an invocation of the immediate-polynomial-obstruction node.

Write $P(x)=x^p-Ax$. The set $S_{A,s}(F)$ is an additive subgroup for $F=K,L$: the binomial identity bounds $|P(x+y)-P(x)-P(y)|$ by $|p|\max(|x|,|y|)^p<s$ whenever $|px^p|,|py^p|<s$, and the same bound shows the sum still has an admissible parameter. Negation is exact for odd $p$; for $p=2$ the extra term is $2x^2$ of norm $<s$. The error terms form the additive ball $|e|<s$. For an inadmissible $c$ one has $|pc^p|\ge s$, hence $|c|^p>s\ge r^{p-1}s^{1/p}$ and $|c|^p>|Ac|$. If additionally $|g(c)|<|b|$, cancellation forces $|c|^p=|b|$, contradicting $|pc^p|\ge s>|pb|$. Consequently all $c$ with $|g(c)|<|b|$ are admissible (in characteristic $p$ all $c$ are admissible). Since $|b|>s$, restricting $c$ to $|pc^p|<s$ leaves the infimum equal to $s$. Adding $e$ with $|e|<s$ leaves each norm $|g(c)|>s$ unchanged. Thus $b+S_{A,s}(K)$ excludes zero and has infimum $s$. Moreover $0=g(\theta)-g(\theta)\in b+S_{A,s}(L)$, since both $\theta$ and the error $-g(\theta)$ satisfy their strict bounds.

If $A=0$, keep $a=0$, $s,b$. Otherwise set $n=p-1$. Divisibility of $\Gamma_K$ gives $q\in K^\times$ with $|q|^n=|A|$. The element $u=A/q^n$ has norm one. Algebraic closedness of $\widetilde K$ gives a nonzero residue root of $X^n-\widetilde u$; choose a lift $z_0\in K^\circ$ of this root. For $H(X)=X^n-u$ all coefficients have norm at most one, $|H(z_0)|<1$, $|z_0|=1$ and $|H'(z_0)|=|nz_0^{n-1}|=1$, since $p\nmid n$. Apply [lem-trf-complete-ultrametric-simple-root-lifting]. The lifted root $z$ has $z^n=u$, so $t=qz$ satisfies $t^{p-1}=A$ and $|t|=r$. No base extension was made.

In the second case replace $(A,b,s)$ by $(a,b',s')=(1,b/t^p,1)$. For $F=K,L$ the substitution $c=td$, $e=t^p e'$ gives exactly $t^{-p}S_{A,s}(F)=S_{1,1}(F)$: indeed $t^{-p}(c^p-Ac+e)=d^p-d+e'$, and both strict bounds divide by $|t|^p=s$. Thus the coset's norms and infimum divide by $s$, zero membership is preserved, and $|pb'|<1$. Rename $b',s'$ as $b,s$. In the first case there is no change. We have the required special coset $C=b+S_{a,s}(K)$, split over $L$, with $|a|\le s^{(p-1)/p}$ and $|pb|<s$.

Take any $v\in C$, say $v=b+d^p-ad+e$ with $|pd^p|,|e|<s$. The bound on $a$ gives $|ad|\le\max(s,|d|^p)$, so $|pad|\le\max(|p|s,|pd^p|)<s$. Hence $|pv|<s$. The subgroup identity gives $v+S_{a,s}(K)=C$, whose infimum is $s$ and whose elements have norm at least $s$. Thus the infimum of $|c^p-ac+v|$ over admissible $c$ is $s$: adding a term of norm $<s$ does not change these norms. If an inadmissible $c$ had $|c^p-ac+v|<s$, then $|c|^p>s$ and $|c|^p>|ac|$, forcing $|c|^p=|v|$, contrary to $|pv|<s\le|pc^p|$. This proves the unrestricted infimum is $s$. Also $v+S_{a,s}(L)=b+S_{a,s}(L)$ contains zero, yielding $\alpha\in L$ with $|p\alpha^p|<s$ and $|\alpha^p-a\alpha+v|<s$.

Suppose $a=1$, so $s=1$, and choose the preceding $\alpha$. Expand $H(Y)=(\alpha+Y)^p-(\alpha+Y)+v$. It is monic with constant coefficient of norm $<1$. For $1\le i<p$, the binomial coefficient is divisible by $p$. If $|\alpha|\ge1$, then $|\binom pi\alpha^{p-i}|\le|p||\alpha|^p<1$; if $|\alpha|<1$, this is bounded by $|p|<1$. Therefore all coefficients are integral and the linear coefficient $p\alpha^{p-1}-1$ has norm one. Apply [lem-trf-complete-ultrametric-simple-root-lifting] over the complete field $L$ at $Y=0$ to obtain a zero $y$ of norm $<1$. Then $\beta=\alpha+y\in L$ satisfies $\beta^p-\beta+v=0$. The infimum already proved is one, so this polynomial has no root in $K$; hence $\beta\notin K$. Products of a basis of $L$ over $K(\beta)$ with a basis of $K(\beta)$ over $K$ form a $K$-basis of $L$ (expand coefficients to span and use linear independence successively). Thus $p=[L:K]=[L:K(\beta)][K(\beta):K]$. Since $\beta\notin K$ and $p$ is prime, $K(\beta)=L$. Rename $\beta$ as the requested $\alpha$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q74-715a6acc3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Temkin arXiv:0707.3953v3, section 6.1, printed pp. 36-41, from a pdftotext copy; the local PDF is missing and the worker reported it as WANTED. That covers the definitions of S_{a,s}, critical and special cosets, Lemma 6.1.2 and its Hensel proof, and Prop 6.1.4 with its immediate-case proof (shrinking E_0, |a_1|<=r_0^{p-1}, |a_i|<r^p/r_0^i, |p|r_0^p<r^p, truncation to g, then (ii) and (iii)). The item statement is unchanged and is 6.1.4(i)-(iii) plus 6.1.2(i) for every representative. The tame base change K(a^{1/(p-1)}) is trivial here because the residue field is algebraically closed and the value group divisible; step 4 proves this. New node lem-trf-immediate-minpoly-coefficient-preparation is true: r is positive and not attained by immediacy, |f(c)|=|theta-c|^p by uniqueness of the extended absolute value, |b|=R^p, and the bounds come from shrinking R toward r with |a_i| fixed, including the conditional |a_1|R<r^p. Edge cases checked: inseparable char p (f=T^p-theta^p) and p=2. It holds only the first half of Temkin's proof, so it does not restate the item, and lem-trf-immediate-prime-polynomial-obstruction (no L, no coefficient bounds) is not a duplicate. New node lem-trf-complete-ultrametric-simple-root-lifting is the Newton/Hensel step for a complete real-valued field. It differs from lem-per-henselian-simple-root-stability (henselian, starts from a simple root). No DAG or Mathlib duplicate: Mathlib's Hensel results are the henselian-ring API and hensels_lemma over Z_p only. Steps 1-7 are each checked in review.md. Step 1: the truncation error is below s on |x|<=R. Step 2: inf|g|=s is not attained, by cases |c|<=R and |c|>R. Step 3: subgroup property (binomial terms; 2c^2 for p=2), inadmissible c are excluded via |pb|<s, and the coset splits over L via theta and -g(theta). Step 4: the (p-1)st root via the lifting node, with p not dividing p-1. Step 5: rescaling t^{-p}S_{A,s}=S_{1,1}. Step 6: |pv|<s using |a|<=s^{(p-1)/p}, and the unrestricted infimum equals s. Step 7: H(Y)=(alpha+Y)^p-(alpha+Y)+v has integral coefficients with linear coefficient of norm one; lifting over complete L, beta not in K, and the tower law give L=K(beta). Every non-elementary input is a cited node statement. No cycle, no off-unit tool use, blueprint from/via/same_as consistent, no SGA. No fixes.
